Why does everyone hate it? How does it affect the healthcare market?

I'm not an expert, but it caused rates to go up, you can get fined or sent to jail if you don't sign up, the premium in my state is so high you'd have to be in the hospital for like 3 weeks before it kicks in. Like I said, I'm not an expert.

There are many reasons. I'm self-employed, and as long as I can show my AGI is under $30k annually, I am exempt from fines. However, my AGI has to be under $12k annually to get Medicaid (I live in a state that does not honor the 135% above poverty level thing).

So, here are my options: get ACA's insurance, which right now only approves Blue Cross in my state (not sure how it works in other states). I would have to pay $460 per month for bare bones insurance, along with a $7k annual deductible. Just to cover myself. Or, once the exemptions are removed/phased out, I can pay 9% of my income as a penalty. Right now, I don't have health insurance because it's cheaper than the $5k in insurance premiums plus up to $7k extra to meet deductible. Also, I'm under 35 and fairly healthy. No point in paying that much for an annual physical, I'm insured by my company in case of an accident at work and by my auto insurance in case I'm driving.

If I try to get insurance for my small staff and myself, their premiums are $650 a month for crap health and dental, and I match 50% plus my own premium, so I get to pay a minimum of $975 per month. I can deduct what I match, but is has to be at least half of what they pay. Employees don't even want it, because they couldn't afford it.

I'm meeting with a benefits design company this week to look into getting non-ACA health insurance. Since the company is small enough, I think we could find something more affordable. However, every insurance agent I've spoken to about it has said costs are going to continue to skyrocket, since Obamacare has essentially created a monopoly on healthcare. There are 5 companies left in my area offering health insurance, and only Blue Cross is "ACA compliant".

Those who work low-wage jobs get away with $50 a month for decent care, but people like me have to subsidize the costs. Which, if you think about it, scares people into going out on their own, creating less competition in all markets. No competition = less incentive for innovation, and so on and so forth.

Basically it translates to something along the following lines:

"Rather than actually institute a system where people can either afford healthcare or get it for free, we'll just make it illegal not to have it. That should fix everything!"

Example: I make about $32,000/year. The cheapest healthcare plan I can find with Obamacare is $120/mo, and that's "Catastrophic Coverage" which essentially won't help me in 99.9% of cases because the deductible is like $6,000. So essentially I'd be paying $120/mo for nothing. Fuck that.

Government mandated purchase from a private corporation.

The Government should not be able to force anyone to purchase anything. The people didn't want the product so the companies were going under until big daddy stepped in with his band aid and fixed the issue... If any of us gets sick we are just as fucked as if we didn't have insurance at all. (except me because the VA covers my broke ass)
